post.caption: Sterling silver is only 92.5 percent silver. The other 7.5 percent is usually copper, because pure silver is too soft, and copper adds strength. A 925 stamp means 925 parts silver per thousand. In 1697 England added a purer standard, called Britannia silver, which aimed to stop people melting coins for silverware. Silver tarnishes when sulfur gases in the air react with it, and polishing removes a little silver each time. The word sterling may come from a coin stamped with a star. Until 1920, British silver coins were sterling silver.
